title: Symbol
summary: A symbol is an atomic mark or token admitted by a formal language.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal language context is fixed.

content.plain: A symbol is an atomic mark or token admitted by a formal language.
content.exact: A formal alphabet Σ is a set of distinguishable tokens. Symbols acquire syntactic roles from formation rules and meaning only through an interpretation.
content.example: The glyph + can be a binary function symbol before any meaning is assigned to it.
content.caveat: A glyph, token, and interpreted mathematical object are different layers.
